SCENE 01 — 3 seconds (provisional)
Setting and framing: Medium-wide full-body view at Sol's face height, angled slightly down onto a simple woodland clearing. Sol occupies 36% of frame height at x=28%, with feet at y=74%; a small burning fallen bough is at x=74%, y=67%. Separate foreground earth, a middle-ground charred trunk and distant sage foliage into overlapping painted layers. Keep the lower fifth quiet.
Lighting: Soft overcast daylight from upper-left; cream earth, muted sage and teal distance, honey-brown wood. The existing wood fire adds only a faint localized warm tint.
Camera in generation: Generation: stable camera.
Editing: No camera move planned.
First frame: Sol faces the bough in a shallow three-quarter orientation, both tiny feet planted and short arms lowered. Both original eyes are visible. A clear gap separates his body from the small faceless painted flame rooted on the wood.

Sol: “Who actually discovered fire?”

Action: Sol lifts the short arm nearest the burning bough once into the supplied small presenting position. Keep its original length and attachment point. Let the movement give his painted flame body a small soft bounce: the tip and side lobes follow through with one damped wobble, and the nested color layers and face travel coherently with the body. Keep both stubby feet supported, the normal original oval eye design, with a brief natural blink allowed, and the other arm without a separate gesture. Settle into the approved ending pose and hold.

Last frame: Only Sol's short arm nearest the bough is raised into the approved small presenting position, retaining its length and attachment point. His other arm, body orientation toward the bough, facial markings, silhouette, flame layers and planted feet remain unchanged. The separate small flame stays on the wood.
Next cut: Continue from the exact approved ending asset into Scene 02. Its generated source framing begins unchanged.
